one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event inside the window: the Q3 FY27 print (quarter ended 2026-10-31), expected ~Wed 2026-12-02 after close and so priced in the 2026-12-03 close. The company has not announced the date yet; last year it announced on 2025-11-03 for 2025-12-03 [27], so a notice should come any day. Guide: product 1,588-1,593, non-GAAP op margin 15.5%, 382M shares [6]. The company beat its product guide 10 of 10 quarters (median +4.6%) and its margin guide 10 of 10 (median +3.0 pt). The approved set has 1,617.7 / 16.8%, a smaller beat than usual because the CFO says the guide only forecasts 'observed behavior' and calls ~3% 'a very solid beat' [25], and Observe now sits in the base. A beat is expected (Street EPS 0.60 vs whisper 0.71), so the price reaction turns on the FY27 Q4 implied guide and cRPO/RPO (bookings weighted to Q4 [26]). Risk: a ~286M loss on the 2027-note repurchase could land in Q3 GAAP and possibly non-GAAP other income. Earnings moves have been large (+23% after Q2). I use a lognormal with median 298 (+0.7% drift for the beat habit and post-surprise drift) and sigma 0.20, a little above annual vol / 3.5 = 0.183 because this is an earnings month. Nothing else is scheduled; the macro prints are the 2026-11-07 jobs report and CPI mid-November.

fair_value.method: Approved quarterly driver build (NRR x year-ago product + new-customer revenue; product GM and opex ratio) gives ~9.78B NTM revenue at 2027-11-03. At 11.0x EV/NTM sales plus ~2.5B net cash over 388.7M shares that is $283.3 (weight 0.9); an SBC-burdened owner-earnings leg gives $103.1 (weight 0.1). Blend $265.3.

thesis_break_reason: Around $180 (-39%) the market would be pricing growth near 20% at ~7x NTM sales, i.e. the downside case: TTM NRR rolling below ~122% with product growth under 25%, a product-guide miss after the 10/10 beat record, or product GM sliding toward 70% as AI workloads scale. Ordinary volatility (64% realised) can take the stock to ~$220 without a broken thesis; under ~$180 one of those fundamentals has most likely failed.

reasoning: Lane: primary. I read the Q2 FY27 release and 10-Q, the 2026-10-01 convertible 8-K, the FY25/FY26 Q4 releases (first annual guides), the Q1 FY27 corrected call transcript, the June 2026 Investor Day deck and a summary of the Q2 call. Fetches were limited to 6 under the shared budget, and Twelve Data statistics and estimates are not on this plan. Guidance record: the quarterly product guide was beaten 10/10 (median +4.6%) and the annual first guide by +6.5% (FY25) and +4.5% (FY26). But the FY27 guide has already been raised twice (5,660 -> 6,070), and the CFO says the guide only forecasts 'observed behavior' and that ~3% is 'a very solid beat'. So I accept the approved set's smaller H2 beat (FY27 product 6,136, +1.1% over the guide, ~0.5% over the Street) and do not argue against any driver. My view against the drivers by id: nrr's rise to 128-129% is plausible (TTM lag); the risk is in the FY29-30 fade, which I would not take lower. new_cust's drop from 118 to ~70 a quarter is conservative given 692 net adds and Observe. product_gm 73.5-74.5% is fair after the 75 -> 74% guide cut. opex_pct's leverage is backed by 17 organic hires in Q1. ps_rev doesn't matter. Valuation: the METHOD FIT flag is real. GAAP operating income TTM is -1,237 and SBC 1,642 exceeds FCF 1,195, and among the peers GAAP P/E runs 17x-1287x and FCF-less-SBC yields are ~0-2% (TDC aside), so earnings multiples carry no signal. EV/NTM sales is the operative basis. The 6 filing-based peers give a median of 6.0x; SNOW is at 14.0x, which is growth-explained (DDOG 14.2x at the same 35% growth). The k = 0.8 rule gives 11.8x; I take 11.0x because the approved build slows NTM growth from 32% to 25% by the horizon while the peer group is re-accelerating. That -0.8x is flagged for Kilian (about -6%). I added a non-multiple owner-earnings leg with SBC as a cost. It gives $103 and shows the price depends on SBC falling to ~13% of revenue and margins reaching ~27%. I weight it 0.1 because DCF-like legs tested low. The research target (12m) is $265, 10% under the $295.85 close. Scenarios move the approved drivers (downside nrr -4 pt / new_cust -25% / product_gm -2 pt; upside +3 pt / +20% / +1 pt) and the multiple (7x / 16x). P10 $156 and P90 $410 mean lognormal spreads of 0.41 / 0.34, below the 64% realized vol, which was inflated by the +23% Q2 gap and the run from $118 to $385. Not driver-linked: the custom owner-earnings leg (per-share value from FY30 build figures, stated by hand).

model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) exit EV/sales 11.0x vs the k = 0.8 rule's 11.84x (-0.8x for the build's 7-pt growth deceleration, half of what a log-growth regression across the 6 peers implies, b = 0.067 per growth point): moves the research target ~-6% (11.84x gives ~$304 on the multiple leg vs $283). The full regression reading (~9.7-10.0x) would give ~$258. (2) The 0.1-weight owner-earnings leg (103) pulls the blend ~-18; at weight 0 the target is ~283. (3) Net debt at H rolls with FCFF = NOPAT only (the set has no D&A, capex, deferred-revenue or buyback rows): actual adj FCF runs above non-GAAP operating income (FY27 adj FCF guide 23% [25] vs 14.5% margin), so net cash at H may be ~0.7-1.0B higher (~+$2-3/share), partly spent on buybacks ($802.7M authorization left through March 2027 [7]). (4) Possible Q3 non-GAAP EPS hit from the ~286 loss on the 2027-note repurchase (set flag). (5) Greenshoe on the new notes (up to $550M) not disclosed as exercised: ~neutral to net cash. Financing below 20%: no further raise expected (net cash 1.3B, FCF positive).
